1.text:
The chapter opens with one compact utterance, “Alif-Lãm-Mĩm-Ṣãd,” and does not attach an explanation to it in the verse. The letters come before any description of the Book, any warning, or any instruction to the hearers. That placement matters because the next verse moves straight to a Book sent down to the Prophet and names its purpose. The opening therefore begins with a form the reader can recite without being told here exactly how to interpret it, then turns to the guidance that follows. The chapter will later describe earlier messengers and communities, their responses, and what follows from those responses. The contrast between the brief opening and the long account that follows gives the chapter a clear movement: it starts with words that remain unexplained here, then develops the message and its consequences.

**The letters and their meaning.**

Al-Jalālayn leaves the letters at the limit of what can be explained here: God knows best what He means by them. Ibn Kathīr says he has discussed the explanation of these letters earlier, while Al-Mukhtaṣar specifically points back to al-Baqarah. Those comments direct the reader to prior discussion rather than supplying a new explanation in this verse. They also keep the four letters together as the opening given here, without making one proposed expansion the verse's settled meaning.

**The readings offered by Tanwīr.**

Tanwīr al-Miqbās transmits one reading through Ibn ʿAbbās: “I am Allah Who knows best and is best.” It then preserves another possibility, that the letters form an oath by which Allah swore. The two possibilities are not identical. The first takes the sounds as words that can be expanded into a statement about divine knowledge and goodness. The other treats them as the beginning of an oath. The source gives both readings without resolving between them, so neither should be presented as the only explanation.

**The chapter's themes.**

Maʿārif-ul-Qurʾān's overview puts the chapter's opening alongside its broad themes of the Hereafter and prophethood. It describes the opening portion as concerned with those subjects before the chapter turns to detailed accounts of earlier prophets, their communities, their reward, and the punishment that overtook them. Tazkirul Qurʾān describes the Book as guidance and as a warning to those who reject it, while noting that some receive its guidance and others treat it as unreal. That contrast anticipates the chapter's recurring movement between a messenger's call and a community's response. The opening letters are therefore not a replacement for the message that follows; the following verse introduces the Book and its work of warning and reminding.

2.text:
“This is a Book sent down to you O Prophet” names both the message and the one charged with carrying it. The next phrase, “do not let anxiety into your heart regarding it,” addresses the inward strain that may come when hearers resist what is delivered. The verse does not make the Prophet responsible for making every listener believe; it turns that concern toward the work itself. “so with it you may warn the disbelievers” gives the Book a warning role for those who reject it, while “and as a reminder to the believers” identifies the hearers who are ready to take its guidance. The same message is therefore presented in two ways, a warning where there is refusal and a reminder where there is faith. The verse moves from revelation, through the messenger's burden, to the people the Book addresses. The next command turns to what these hearers must do: follow what has come from their Lord rather than take other protectors beside Him. The message is not only a burden for the Prophet, since the verse also names the people who will hear it. Some are to be warned, and believers are to be reminded. The following command turns from the messenger to those hearers and sets following what is revealed against taking other protectors. The verse does not treat these purposes as competing, but places them side by side.

**The constraint in conveying the Book.**

This is a Book that is revealed to you — addressing the Prophet s — so let there be no inhibition no constraint in your breast because of it to convey it — for fear that you might be called a liar — that you may warn thereby li-tundhira ‘that you may warn’ is semantically connected to unzila ‘is revealed’ that is to say ‘it is revealed for the purposes of warning’ and as a reminder for those who believe in it. (haraj) translated here as constraint' means that you should have no anguish or apprehension in conveying the Qur'an and its injunctions lest people belie it and hurt you.' (As reported from Abu Al- Aliyah - Mazhari) The hint given here is that Allah who has sent down this Book on you has also made arrangements that you shall remain protected and that takes care of any anguish on your part. Some commentators have said that haraj' or constraint on the heart' refers to the constraint experienced by the Holy Prophet who, because of his affectionate concern for people, felt pain when they would not believe despite having heard the Qur'an and its injunctions. (so let not your breast be narrow therefrom,) meaning, having doubt about it according to Mujahid, Qatadah and As-Suddi. It was also said that the meaning here is: 'do not hesitate to convey the Qur'an and warn with it,'.

**The warning and the reminder.**

((It is) a Scripture) this Scripture, i.e. the Qur'an (that is revealed unto thee (Muhammad) that Gabriel brought to you (so let there be no heaviness in thy heart) let there be no doubt in your heart (therefrom) i.e. there can be no doubt about the Qur'an being from Allah (that thou mayst warn thereby) that you may warn the people of Makkah through the Qur'an in order that they believe, (and (it is) a Reminder unto believers). He revealed it to you to warn people by it and to be a proof, and to remind those who have faith through it, because it is they who benefit from being reminded. The Book of God is, in essence, a book of guidance. For the others it amounts only to a warning of the impending grievous fate towards which they are moving because of their arrogance.

**The Prophet's duty and the people's response.**

To offset this constraint, the Holy Prophet has been told that the duty with which he has been obligated is simply to make the call and convey the message. Once this is done, it is not his responsibility to see who becomes a Muslim and who does not. Therefore, there was no reason for him to be anxious. (Follow what has been sent down unto you from your Lord) meaning, follow and imitate the unlettered Prophet , who brought you a Book that was revealed for you, from the Lord and master of everything. (and follow not any Awliya', besides Him (Allah) meaning, do not disregard what the Messenger brought you and follow something else, for in this case, you will be deviating from Allah's judgment to the decision of someone else.

3.text:
“Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord” begins with a direction, not a suggestion. The source of the message is given as the reason it should guide the hearer. “and do not take others as guardians besides Him” marks the boundary: following revelation cannot be combined with giving other protectors the authority that belongs to God. These first two phrases set a positive act beside its opposite, accepting the guidance and refusing to replace it. “How seldom are you mindful” then turns the commands into a rebuke. The issue is not that the words are hard to hear, but that people do not keep their force in mind. This follows the preceding verse's description of warning and reminder: hearers who receive a reminder are now called to act on it, and the next passage begins showing the outcome when a community fails to do so. The verse thus brings the reader from what the Book offers to the choice it names. Its last words do not soften the instruction; they expose the gap between having the message and living by it.

**The Prophet's duty and the audience's choice.**

Some commentators have said that haraj' or constraint on the heart' refers to the constraint experienced by the Holy Prophet who, because of his affectionate concern for people, felt pain when they would not believe despite having heard the Qur'an and its injunctions. To offset this constraint, the Holy Prophet has been told that the duty with which he has been obligated is simply to make the call and convey the message. Once this is done, it is not his responsibility to see who becomes a Muslim and who does not. Therefore, there was no reason for him to be anxious. Say to them Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord namely the Qur’ān and do not follow do not take beside Him namely God in other words other than Him any patrons obeying them in disobedience of Him exalted be He. (Follow what has been sent down unto you from your Lord) meaning, follow and imitate the unlettered Prophet , who brought you a Book that was revealed for you, from the Lord and master of everything. Follow, O people, the Scripture which your Lord revealed to you, and the traditions of your Prophet.

**Other guardians and protection.**

(and follow not any Awliya', besides Him (Allah) meaning, do not disregard what the Messenger brought you and follow something else, for in this case, you will be deviating from Allah's judgment to the decision of someone else. ((Saying): Follow that which is sent down unto you from your Lord) i.e. the Qur'an: uphold as lawful that which it makes lawful and unlawful that which it makes unlawful, (and follow) and worship (no protecting friends) idols as lords (beside Him. Little do you recollect) you do not take admonition neither much nor a little! Do not follow the desires of those you imagine to be friends and protectors amongst the devils or evil scholars, turning to them and leaving what was revealed to you because of your desires.

**Remembering, rejection, and truth.**

Little do you remember read tadhakkarūn or yadhakkarūn ‘little are you or they admonished’; the original tā’ of tatadhakkarūn has been assimilated with the dhāl; a variant reading has tadhkurūn; the mā of qalīlan mā ‘little’ is extra merely emphasising the ‘littleness’. If you had remembered, you would not have preferred falsehood over the truth, and you would have followed what your Messenger came with, acting in obedience to it and leaving anything besides it. Here everybody has the opportunity and the liberty to accept or reject the truth as he pleases, and even find clever words to justify his stand. As soon as the period of trial comes to an end, it will be revealed to all that the preacher’s words were based on eternal truths; that it was sheer bias and egotism on his opponents’ part which prevented them from seeing the Truth at the core of his arguments. It will become clear at that time that the arguments advanced by them to contradict the preacher’s words were simply a falsification of the facts and not a form of reasoning in any real sense. (And most of mankind will not believe even if you desire it eagerly)[12:103], and;. (And if you obey most of those on the earth, they will mislead you far away from Allah's path)[6:116], and,.

4.text:
“Imagine how many societies We have destroyed!” opens by asking the listener to picture not one case but many. The following phrase, “Our torment took them by surprise while sleeping at night or midday,” makes the danger sudden and places it at times of rest, when people would not expect to be called to account. The verse does not name the societies here or recount each history; it states the recurring pattern in a single line. The next verse supplies their response, an admission that they had done wrong. This ordering matters: the warning is first presented as a fact about communities that seemed secure, then as a moment when their past choices can no longer be denied. The two times named cover night and the middle of the day, so the point is not a fixed hour but the unexpected arrival of the punishment. The verse turns the warning in the previous command into a concrete example. Its question asks the hearer to compare the ordinary rhythm of life with the sudden end described here.

**The towns that were destroyed.**

How many kam is predicative and is the direct object of the main verb ahlaknāhā ‘We have destroyed’ a city meaning its inhabitants have We destroyed have We willed its destruction! (And a great number of towns We destroyed.) for defying Our Messengers and rejecting them. This behavior led them to earn disgrace in this life, which led them to disgrace in the Hereafter. (And many a township did We destroy while they were given to wrongdoing, so that it lie in ruins (up to this day), and (many) a deserted well and lofty castle!)[22:45], and,. (How many a town given to wrongdoing, have We destroyed)[21:11], until,. (How many a township) people of townships (have We destroyed) We tormented! How many cities Allah has destroyed through His punishment because they persisted in their disbelief and error!

**The timing of the punishment.**

So Our might Our chastisement came upon it at night or while they slept at noon qā’ilūn al-qaylūla is a rest taken halfway during the day even if it does not involve sleep in other words sometimes it came upon it at night and sometimes it came during the day. (Our torment came upon them by night or while they were taking their midday nap.) means, Allah's command, torment and vengeance came over them at night or while taking a nap in the middle of the day. Both of these times are periods of rest and leisure or heedlessness and amusement. (Did the people of the towns then feel secure against the coming of Our punishment by night while they were asleep? Or, did the people of the towns then feel secure against the coming of Our punishment in the forenoon while they were playing?)[7:97-98] and,. (As a raid by night) or day, (or while they slept at noon, Our terror) Our punishment (came unto them). Allah sent His punishment down on them in their obliviousness at night or during the day: they could not do anything to avoid the punishment, and their false gods could do nothing to protect them from it. Our torment came upon them by night or while they were taking their midday nap No cry did they utter when Our torment came upon them but this:

**The world's measure and the truth.**

In this world the importance of an individual is gauged by the material splendour surrounding him, and his ability to influence people with his impressive words, and thus have a massive following. Since the preacher is not generally in such a happy position, his word is valueless in the eyes of worldly people, while the words of his opponents, who bask in material grandeur have a greater impact. But when Doomsday uncovers all the facts, the position will be just the opposite. Now, all the weight will be on the side of the Truth: Untruth will be divested of all its arguments and will be rendered valueless. (And indeed (many) Messengers before you were mocked at, but their scoffers were surrounded by the very thing that they used to mock at)[6:10], and.

5.text:
“Their only cry, when overwhelmed by Our torment, was” introduces the response after the sudden destruction just described. The words do not give a list of excuses or a dispute about what happened. They give one admission, “We have indeed been wrongdoers,” so the scene moves from punishment to recognition of guilt. The confession cannot undo the injustice that brought the torment, but it makes clear that the people know how their conduct should be named. The next verses turn from their answer to questions addressed to communities and messengers, so this admission sits within a larger account of deeds, response, and responsibility. Its position after the destruction matters: the acknowledgement comes only when there is no way to hide the wrong that preceded it.

**The words left after the torment.**

And their only plea their only words when Our might came upon them was to say ‘We were evildoers indeed’. (No cry did they utter when Our torment came upon them but this: "Verily, we were wrongdoers.") This means, when the torment came to them, their cry was that they admitted their sins and that they deserved to be punished. (No plea) words (had they, when Our terror) Our punishment which destroyed them (came unto them, save that they said: Lo! We were wrong-doers) idolaters. All they could do when the punishment came down on them was to admit that they had done wrong through their disbelief in Allah.

**Wrongdoing and rejection.**

(No cry did they utter when Our torment came upon them but this: "Verily, we were wrongdoers.") (No plea) words (had they, when Our terror) Our punishment which destroyed them (came unto them, save that they said: Lo! We were wrong-doers) idolaters. All they could do when the punishment came down on them was to admit that they had done wrong through their disbelief in Allah. (And a great number of towns We destroyed.) for defying Our Messengers and rejecting them. This behavior led them to earn disgrace in this life, which led them to disgrace in the Hereafter. Since the preacher is not generally in such a happy position, his word is valueless in the eyes of worldly people, while the words of his opponents, who bask in material grandeur have a greater impact. But when Doomsday uncovers all the facts, the position will be just the opposite.

**The questions that follow.**

Then surely, We shall question those (people) to whom it was sent and verily, We shall question the Messengers Then surely, We shall narrate unto them (their whole story) with knowledge, and indeed We have not been absent. (Then surely, We shall question those (people) to whom it (the Book) was sent) is similar to the Ayat,. (And (remember) the Day (Allah) will call them, and say: "What answer gave you to the Messengers?")[28:65], and,. Allah will question the nations, on the Day of Resurrection, how they responded to His Messengers and the Messages He sent them with. He will also question the Messengers if they conveyed His Messages. (Then surely, We shall question those (people) to whom it (the Book) was sent and verily, We shall question the Messengers.) He said; "About what they conveyed.

6.text:
The statement “We will surely question those who received messengers and We will question the messengers themselves” places both communities and messengers before the final reckoning. The two groups are kept in view, with attention to how communities responded and whether messengers delivered the message. The verse repeats the act of questioning, but the questions concern different responsibilities. It follows the confession in the previous verse: the wrongdoing people admit is now placed within a larger examination of what they did with guidance and how it reached them. The next verse gives an account with knowledge and makes clear that nothing was absent. Here the text marks the two groups whose actions will be addressed.

**The communities' response.**

Then verily We shall question those to whom the Message was sent that is We shall question those communities about their response to the messengers and to what extent they implemented that which was conveyed to them; and We shall question the messengers about the conveying of that Message. The statement: ‌ ‌ 6 in verse 6 refers to the day of Qiyamah when people will be asked by Allah how did they receive the messengers and Books sent to them by Him - and the messengers will be asked if they did convey to their communities the message and injunctions Allah had sent them with. Allah will question the nations, on the Day of Resurrection, how they responded to His Messengers and the Messages He sent them with. Allah will certainly question the communities He sent messengers to on the Day of Judgement: about how they received the messengers.

**The messengers and their delivery.**

Then verily We shall question those to whom the Message was sent that is We shall question those communities about their response to the messengers and to what extent they implemented that which was conveyed to them; and We shall question the messengers about the conveying of that Message. He will also question the Messengers if they conveyed His Messages. We shall question these people about their response to the messengers, (and verily We shall question the messengers) about their conveyance of the message. Also, He will certainly question the messengers about whether they delivered what they were instructed to deliver, and how their communities responded to it.

**The message and its conveyance.**

When, on the day of Qiyamah, you will be asked about me - whether or not I have conveyed the message of Allah to you - what will you, then, say in reply? (Then surely, We shall question those (people) to whom it (the Book) was sent and verily, We shall question the Messengers.) He said; "About what they conveyed. Therefore, all of you should make sure that those who are present do convey my message to those absent. Those absent' refers to people who were present during that time but were not present at that particular occasion - as well as generations which would come later on.

7.text:
“Then We will give them a full account with sure knowledge” completes the sequence of questioning. It does not describe a report pieced together from witnesses; the account is described as known in full. “for We were never absent” explains why nothing in that account can be missing: the actions and the delivery of the message took place under knowledge that was never absent from them. The opening “Then” ties this verse to the questions about communities and messengers in the one before it. Together the verses move from what each group did to an account of those actions. The point is not only that judgment comes later, but that it addresses real responses and real acts of delivery. The next verse turns to the balance of deeds, so the account of what people did is followed by an image of how their deeds are weighed. Nothing here leaves room for a gap between what was asked, what was done, and what is finally made known. The deeds, questions, and account remain together in this passage.

**Nothing is absent from the account.**

And We shall narrate to them with knowledge We shall inform them with previous knowledge of what they did; for verily We were not absent when the messengers were conveying the Message nor were We absent during the time of bygone communities and what they did. (Then verily We shall narrate unto them) inform them (with knowledge) with elucidation, (for verily We were not absent) from the conveyance of the messengers and the response of the people (when it came to pass). Nothing is hidden from Him, and He was never, at any point, absent from them. Certainly, He witnesses to everything, nothing escapes His observation, and He is never unaware of anything. Rather, He has perfect knowledge of what the eyes are deluded by and what the hearts conceal,.

**What is made known on the Day of Resurrection.**

(Then surely, We shall narrate unto them (their whole story) with knowledge, and indeed We have not been absent.) "The Book will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and it will speak, disclosing what they used to do." (and indeed We have not been absent) meaning, On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will inform His servants about what they said and did, whether substantial or minor. The statement: ‌ ‌ 6 in verse 6 refers to the day of Qiyamah when people will be asked by Allah how did they receive the messengers and Books sent to them by Him - and the messengers will be asked if they did convey to their communities the message and injunctions Allah had sent them with.

**Who carries the message forward.**

When, on the day of Qiyamah, you will be asked about me - whether or not I have conveyed the message of Allah to you - what will you, then, say in reply? Therefore, all of you should make sure that those who are present do convey my message to those absent. Those absent' refers to people who were present during that time but were not present at that particular occasion - as well as generations which would come later on. To convey to them the message of the Holy Prophet means that people of every time should continue the chain of conveying this message to the generations coming next, so that all children of Adam to be born right through the day of Qiyamah will have received this message.

8.text:
“The weighing on that Day will be just” establishes the standard before the verse describes either outcome. The balance is not governed by reputation or the claims people make for themselves, but by justice in the weighing of deeds. “As for those whose scale will be heavy with good deeds” shifts from the rule to one group and names the feature that marks their outcome. “only they will be successful” closes that movement by connecting a heavy scale with success. The verse gives a measure, a result, and a judgment about who reaches safety. It follows the statement that every deed will be known and weighed, and the next verse describes the opposite condition, a scale that is light. The contrast is not between visible standing in this life, but between the deeds that will be present on that Day. That order makes the result depend on the weighing rather than on what people claimed about themselves. The scale therefore connects the weighing of deeds with the result the verse names. This keeps the scale and the judgment in view together.

**What is weighed.**

The weighing of deeds or of the scrolls of these deeds shall be — in a balance that has a tongue and two palms as scales as reported in a hadīth — on that day that is on the day of the questioning mentioned namely the Day of Resurrection the true weighing the fair weighing al-haqq ‘the true’ is an adjectival qualification of al-wazn ‘the weighing’. Now, if Allah Almighty, the Maker of makers, in His perfect power, could weigh or measure human deeds - with or without a device - what is there in it which would make it to be something far out to believe? Out of the details on the weighing of deeds appearing in the Ahadith of the Holy Prophet the first to ponder about is the oft-narrated statement that, on the day of Resurrection, the heaviest in weight shall be the Kalimah: As for what will be placed on the Balance on the Day of Resurrection, it has been said that the deeds will be placed on it, even though they are not material objects. Allah will give these deeds physical weight on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that the Book of Records that contains the deeds will be weighed. It is also possible to combine the meanings of these Ayat and Hadiths by stating that all this will truly occur, for sometimes the deeds will be weighed, sometimes the scrolls where they are recorded will be weighed, and sometimes those who performed the deeds will be weighed.

**Justice in the weighing.**

(will be the true (weighing), for Allah will not wrong anyone. (And We shall set up the Balances of justice on the Day of Resurrection, then none will be dealt with unjustly in anything. And if there be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And Sufficient are We to take account.)[21:47],. The weighing of what they did on the Day of Judgement will be with justice, with no one being wronged in the least.

**The heavy scale and success.**

So, as for those whose scale (of good deeds) will be heavy, they will be the successful (by entering Paradise)And as for those whose scale will be light, they are those who will lose themselves for their wrongful behavior with Our Ayat. (Then as for him whose scale (of good deeds) will be heavy. He will live a pleasant life (in Paradise). But as for him whose scale (of good deeds) will be light. He will have his home in Hawiyah (pit, Hell). And what will make you know what it is? (It is) a fiercely blazing Fire!)[101:6-11] and,. On the day of Qiyamah, there will come some heavy people whose weight, in the sight of Allah, will not be worth the weight of even a mosquito - and, in support, he recited the verse of the Qur'an: In it, it is said that there are two words very light when said but very heavy when weighed on the Scale of Deeds, and with Allah, they are dear, and they are: Those whose good actions weigh more than their bad actions have succeeded in reaching the goal and being saved from what they feared. The weighing of deeds with the scales of self-purification is true, and the weighing of states with the scales of truthfulness is just. Hapless and deprived is he whose deeds are tainted with eye service and whose states are mixed with self-admiration, for in the station of the scales these states will have no value and those deeds will have no weight. "Take an accounting of yourselves before you are brought to account, weigh your deeds before they are weighed, and prepare for the Greatest Exposure. " He is saying, "Weigh your own deeds before they are weighed against you, take an account of yourself and gaze upon your own works: What have you made ready for the Greatest Exposure and the gathering place of the resurrection? " This is why the Lord of the Worlds said, "Let every soul consider what it has forwarded for tomorrow" [59:18].

9.text:
“But those whose scale is light” turns directly to the opposite side of the balance described in the previous verse. The verse connects that lightness with the loss of the people themselves, not just the loss of a reward. “they have doomed themselves for wrongfully denying Our signs” gives the reason for that loss: their denial is set against the signs they were given. The scale is thus a picture of the outcome of a course they chose, while the final phrase identifies that course as a refusal of the message. This is not a separate group from the one just described by a difference of status; it is the contrasting result of deeds and response. The verse does not present the loss as accidental or unexplained; it ties it to that denial. The movement from the heavier scale to the lighter one makes the standard clear before the chapter returns to the world and its provisions. It links the scale, the deeds, and the final loss to their denial here.

**How the light scale is measured.**

And as for those whose scales are light because of evil deeds those are the ones who have lost their souls by causing them to travel towards the Fire because they mistreated they knowingly denied Our signs. Then, all those Books of Deeds full of sins will be placed in one scale-pan and in the other, this note with the Kalimah of 'Iman on it. The scale-pan with the Kalimah on it shall weigh heavier and the scale-pan with all those sins on it shall turn to be lighter. The one whose scale-pan with good deeds is heavier will have his salvation while the one whose scale-pan with sins and evils is heavier will have his punishment. So, as for those whose scale (of good deeds) will be heavy, they will be the successful (by entering Paradise)And as for those whose scale will be light, they are those who will lose themselves for their wrongful behavior with Our Ayat. As for what will be placed on the Balance on the Day of Resurrection, it has been said that the deeds will be placed on it, even though they are not material objects. Allah will give these deeds physical weight on the Day of Resurrection. It is also possible to combine the meanings of these Ayat and Hadiths by stating that all this will truly occur, for sometimes the deeds will be weighed, sometimes the scrolls where they are recorded will be weighed, and sometimes those who performed the deeds will be weighed.

**The light scale and the lost soul.**

(those are they who lose their souls) by being punished (because they disbelieved Our revelations) Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an. Those whose bad actions weigh more than their good actions are the people who have lost themselves, gaining their destruction on the Day of Judgement and being excluded from eternal bliss because of their rejection of Allah’s signs and verses. (Then as for him whose scale (of good deeds) will be heavy. He will live a pleasant life (in Paradise). But as for him whose scale (of good deeds) will be light. He will have his home in Hawiyah (pit, Hell). And what will make you know what it is? (It is) a fiercely blazing Fire!)[101:6-11] and,. Whoever has his scale of good deeds heavy will be in life blissful and whoever has his scale of good deeds lighter, his place will be Hell -101:6-9. The believer whose good deeds on the scale are heavier will go to Jannah with his deeds - and the one whose evil deeds on the scale are heavier will be sent to Jahannam with his deeds. In this, the good deeds of one believer will be heavy on the scale while the other will find the scale heavy with evil deeds - and everyone will have his or her punishment or reward in accordance with that.

**Truth and worldly standing.**

In this world the importance of an individual is gauged by the material splendour surrounding him, and his ability to influence people with his impressive words, and thus have a massive following. Since the preacher is not generally in such a happy position, his word is valueless in the eyes of worldly people, while the words of his opponents, who bask in material grandeur have a greater impact. But when Doomsday uncovers all the facts, the position will be just the opposite. Now, all the weight will be on the side of the Truth: Untruth will be divested of all its arguments and will be rendered valueless.

10.text:
“We have indeed established you on earth and provided you with a means of livelihood” turns the passage from the final weighing to life as it is lived now. The verse names two gifts together: a place on earth and the means to sustain life there. Its second phrase, “Yet you seldom give any thanks,” changes the direction of the sentence. What has been provided is followed not by praise but by a rebuke for how rarely gratitude is shown. The contrast makes daily provision part of the same moral account as the deeds weighed in the previous verses. The reference is broad, addressing humanity rather than a single individual. The next verse begins the account of Adam and Iblis, where pride and refusal give a story to the problem of thanklessness introduced here. The verse sets the conditions of human life alongside the response expected of those who benefit from them. Its final word leaves the charge open to every hearer. The verse places provision beside the gratitude expected from those who receive it, and this makes its rebuke reach beyond one moment of need. The provision described is practical: food, drink, clothing, and ways to earn a living are included in what makes life possible on earth.

**Earth and its bounties.**

And surely, We gave you authority on the earth and appointed for you therein livelihoods. All Bounties in the Heavens and Earth are for the Benefit of Mankind. Allah reminds of His favor on His servants in that He made the earth a fixed place for dwelling, placed firm mountains and rivers on it and made homes and allowed them to utilize its benefits. Allah made the clouds work for them (bringing rain) so that they may produce their sustenance from them.

**Livelihood and earnings.**

And We have given you power O Children of Adam in the earth and have appointed for you therein livelihoods ma‘āyish is the plural of ma‘īsha that is the means by which you are able to subsist; little qalīlan mā mā is to emphasise the ‘littleness’ thanks you show for this. (And We have given you (mankind) power in the earth, and appointed for you therein) in the earth (a livelihood) that from which you eat, drink and clothe yourselves. Allah certainly established you, O children of Adam, on the earth, and gave you the means of making a living. He also created the ways and means of earnings, commercial activities and other professions.

**Thanks and the way people respond.**

Yet, most of them give liltle thanks for this. Whatever God has bestowed upon man in this world has been given for the purpose of eliciting his gratitude. But this is the very thing which man does not offer to his Lord. The reason for this is that Satan contrives to distort his feelings and steers him away from any expression of gratitude. On all such occasions man is being judged whether he responds positively or reacts negatively. (Little give you thanks!) you do not give thanks for what is great nor for the small; it is also said that this means: you give little thanks for all that is done for you. You should be thankful to Allah for that, but you give little thanks.

**The worldly test of wealth, rights, and pride.**

It becomes evident from the story of Adam and Satan what the real criterion is for the judgement of one’s case. Man is being judged at the point where feelings of jealousy and pride develop in the human heart. In this world of trial it happens again and again that one man rises above another; sometimes one man receives a greater share of wealth and honour as compared to his fellow men. Sometimes, in a deal between two persons, it happens that one of them considers his discharging of the other’s legitimate rights as degrading to himself.
